title: Hawk Fire Reaches 93% Containment; First Fatality Confirmed as Evacuees Return to Reno
detail: Nevada's Hawk Fire, burning northwest of Reno since Aug. 22, reached 93% containment on 15,085 acres with roughly 570 firefighters assigned, allowing several evacuation zones including stretches of North Valleys to be downgraded to 'safe to return.' The Sacramento County Coroner's Office confirmed the fire's first fatality: 83-year-old Reno resident Hayde Medina-Valiente, who died from injuries sustained in the blaze after being transferred to UC Davis Medical Center. The fire has destroyed 47 homes and one commercial building; officials say it was human-caused. Extended drought and record heat linked to the intensifying El Niño have elevated wildfire risk across the American West.

media.caption: Hawk Fire reaches 93% containment as evacuees begin returning to Reno-area homes
